blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

img.alt: Diagram showing a rodding cable fed through a cleanout access point into the main sewer line, with a cutting head clearing the blockage toward the street connection

blocks.h2: Algonquin Main Line Clog Warning Signs
blocks.intro: These point past one fixture to the main line:

tiles.body: It's the lowest drain in the house, so a main line clog shows there first.

tiles.h3: Gurgling in More Than One Room
tiles.body: Toilets or tubs bubbling when something else drains.

tiles.h3: A Backup When the Washer Empties
tiles.body: The surge of water can't get past the blockage.
A basement shower or toilet that fills or drains slowly.

blocks.intro: More than half of Algonquin homes were built in the 1990s and 2000s, so main line clogs usually come from roots, settling or what goes down the drain.

items.body: Subdivision trees are now big enough to reach sewer lines. Roots get in at joints and form mats.
Where a section settled, water sits and paper and wipes pile up.
Family households send a lot of both down the drain. They bind into plugs.
Roots returning fast call for [hydro jetting](/algonquin/hydro-jetting). A sag or crack calls for a [sewer repair](/algonquin/sewer-repair).

blocks.intro: We don't stop at an open drain.

steps.body: We clear the line, then camera it so you see the cause.
If the camera shows damage, you get options and a price for each.

blocks.h2: Sewer Rodding Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: Is it the main line or just one drain?
items.preview: If the floor drain or several fixtures are involved, it's the main.
items.answer: If one fixture is slow, the clog is usually close to it. If the floor drain backs up or several fixtures gurgle, the main line is blocked.

items.q: How often should a line with roots be rodded?
items.answer: About once a year is typical, ideally before spring. The camera helps us adjust that for your line.

items.preview: Usually in the basement near where the line leaves the house, or just outside.
items.answer: In most Algonquin homes, it's in the basement where the main line leaves the house, or in the yard just outside the foundation. We'll find it.

items.q: Can roots be stopped for good?
items.preview: Only by sealing the joints with a liner or repair.
items.answer: Rodding and jetting clear roots, but they grow back. Sealing the joints with a [trenchless liner](/algonquin/trenchless-sewer-repair) or replacing the section stops them.

items.q: What does sewer rodding cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on access and the clog. The price comes before the work.
items.answer: It depends on where the cleanout is, how long the line is and what's blocking it. We quote a flat rate before we start.
